stimulus: The archaeological site of Paharpur has been excavated multiple times. Sir Alexander Cunningham first visited the site in 1879, and although limited by the (a) ------- owner, he managed to discover the ruins of a square tower. In 1919, the site was officially protected under the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act of (b) -------. Regular excavation began in 1923 through the efforts of the Archaeological Survey of India and institutions in Rajshahi and Kolkata. Later, R. D. Banerjee and K. N. Dikshit supervised further (c) ------- of different parts of the site. After the independence of Bangladesh, the Department of Archaeology resumed work in two phases between 1981 and (d) -------. The site revealed the Somapura Mahavihara, a vast Buddhist monastery with a unique architectural design. Its central (e) ------- still stands out because of its remarkable height and structure. ■■■ ■■■
